CHIEF COMPLAINT
Second opinion regarding right index finger injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Philip Gutierrez is a 50-year-old male presenting for a second opinion regarding a right index finger injury sustained in a motor vehicle accident in March 2026. The patient was a passenger in a car that was rear-ended multiple times, which caused him to hyperextend his right index finger. He reports the finger has been painful and swollen since the injury approximately three months ago. He is unable to make a fist and describes the pain as sometimes unbearable, including with driving. He was previously seen at another orthopedic practice where he underwent occupational therapy and MRI imaging. An injection was initially recommended but then deferred due to concerns about worsening the tear. The patient reports confusion regarding the management plan and feels he is not receiving adequate medical care. He is right-handed and works as an x-ray technician, making use of his right hand essential for his occupation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies diabetes or rheumatoid arthritis. Denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Blood pressure medication. History of reaction to methylprednisolone (itching) and dexamethasone (tachycardia).

ALLERGIES
Reaction to dexamethasone (causes heart to race). Reaction to methylprednisolone (causes itching).

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as an x-ray technician. Right-handed. Drove himself to the appointment.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Pleasant, cooperative, healthy male, no distress. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, 2+ radial pulses bilaterally. Hand exam: No swelling or bruising in the palm. Normal creases. Slightly diminished creases over the PIP of the index finger compared to the middle finger. Index finger rests in approximately 10-degree PIP-flexed position. Tenderness elicited with palpation at the MCP joint area. Mild numbness noted. Full extension and flexion of DIP joint intact. Patient reports pain with passive range of motion and flexion maneuvers, particularly with discomfort described as "tearing" sensation. Able to make a fist. Collateral ligaments intact. Extensors intact.

RESULTS
MRI from 4/24/2021 showed focal soft tissue swelling over the right index MCP joint, partial-thickness tear of the right flexor digitorum superficialis (FDS), and fluid consistent with tenosynovitis around the FDP and FDS tendons. Radial and ulnar collateral ligaments of the index MCP joint were intact, as was the MCP joint capsule. Extensor tendons intact. X-rays of the right hand today (four views) showed no bony abnormalities, joint congruency throughout all lesser digits on the right hand, no soft tissue shadows of concern, and no arthritis.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Post-traumatic severe stenosing tenosynovitis of the right index finger with partial-thickness tear of the flexor digitorum superficialis tendon. The patient has significant scar tissue and inflammation around the FDS tendon blocking excursion of other tendons. Plan includes steroid injection with betamethasone (celestone) 1 cc with lidocaine 0.5 cc to avoid previously problematic dexamethasone and methylprednisolone. Two injection attempts were made; the patient had a dramatic painful reaction to the first attempt with hand withdrawal. Second attempt was completed with minimal bleeding from a small palmar vein. Patient counseled on importance of therapeutic steroid injection. Recommended icing this evening and ibuprofen. Outpatient occupational therapy prescribed once weekly for six weeks with goal of full active and passive range of motion with no restrictions. Patient counseled that pain should improve in 3-5 days with further improvement over the following weeks. Reassured that driving is safe. Patient may require repeat injection. Discussed that collateral ligaments and extensors are intact, so no risk of tearing or breaking bone with appropriate movement.
